source.tables: S2 and S3, PDF pages 5 and 6
source.basis: Historical component-resolved reference, not a validated contemporary vehicle design.

historical_auxiliary.basis: Source-role decomposition of the pre-existing whole-ICE proxy. The reference-equivalent 18/275 mass share preserves its lead burden in full vehicle LCIs; it does not identify an EV battery voltage, capacity, measured mass or replacement count.

boundaries: Replace the whole-ICE proxy only in native BEV/FCEV car production; combustion/hybrid car inventories are unchanged.

Split existing nominal proxy mass into historical auxiliary share 18/275 and mechanical remainder 257/275; preserve their sum, driving specifications and all separate motor, controller, converter, charger, PDU, traction battery and fuel-cell links.

Use only gearbox and cooling material rows from the electric source. Do not copy its motor, controller, charger or cables; existing vehicle modules own those components. Cable coverage within those modules remains a separate issue.

Full vehicle LCIs retain the historical auxiliary battery as a labelled provisional component. The final-energy boundary excludes that common component; this is not a zero-lead statement for all EV equipment.
Assembly energy, water, freight and factory are a mass-allocated proxy from the complete 97.51 kg electric reference. They are not measured gearbox-only manufacturing data.

Manufacturing scrap follows gross minus retained source materials. End-of-life mechanical treatment uses its own retained-material fractions and a generic manual-treatment facility rate of 1.6e-8 unit/kg. Do not use the electronics/motor scrap fractions for mechanical equipment.

End-of-life plastics/rubber use waste-plastic mixture treatment, coolant uses hazardous-waste incineration and the provisional auxiliary battery uses the existing lead-acid scrap market. These are treatment proxies, not measured recycling efficiencies or a future primary/secondary scenario.
Existing combustion-car starter/auxiliary boundary and independent modern low-voltage battery specifications remain follow-up issues.
